chapter: Family band and learning to play
title: Malone, the carnival musician who taught them
summary: Malone taught them to spell and wrote arrangements but kept leaving with the carnivals.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: And then we -- you know, we started buying records, all of us, maybe I'd buy this one and the other one buy another record. Then, you know, we started like that. Then this fellow Malone that I told you that started me off on saxophone, the first one that taught me how to spell, I'd say, you know, "Spell it," but I couldn't read fast. My cousin trumpet player could. But the fellow Malone, we couldn't keep him. He'd been on the circuses and carnivals and everytime, anytime a carnival came to town, he'd be playing with us and everything, but anytime a carnival came to town, we didn't lock him up, when that carnival left, he was with it. So we could never depend on him.
